summary.headline: WeWork India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to INR768.7 crore and EBITDA margin reached 21.2%, with PAT up 67.4% to INR65.8 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter: revenue grew 31.6% YoY and 10.1% QoQ to about INR768.7 crore, and EBITDA rose 37.6% YoY to INR162.9 crore at a 21.2% margin. The company added a record ~11,700 desks in the quarter, taking capacity to 145,300 desks across 85 centres, while occupancy rose 357 bps YoY to 83.7%. Net debt of INR310 crore a year ago turned into net cash of INR23 crore, and ROCE reached 34.5%. Management guided to 150,000-155,000 desks by March 2027, and the company is laying out a 190,000-200,000 seat path. All figures are on an IGAAP-equivalent basis.

segments.name: Core flex / membership
segments.commentary: Core business revenue INR657.7 crore, up 31.7% YoY. Members grew 32.5% to about 121,700, and occupancy reached 83.7% (mature centres ~88%, growth centres 64.8% vs 51.4% a year ago).

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: VAS revenue INR79.6 crore, up 35% YoY; management says VAS is margin accretive. Customization revenue about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital revenue INR29.2 crore, up 46% YoY, operating at close to 80% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Desk count expected at about 150,000-155,000 by March 2027 (145,300 at Sept 30; ~4,500 added by Oct 5, so already ~150,000); some March deliveries could slip to early April.
Longer term: path to about 190,000-200,000 seats, with FY28 and FY29 supply under negotiation; management says FY28 rollout will be higher than FY27.
Margins: Q3 and Q4 to see further expansion as occupancy rises, with larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire; capacity additions lower in the next two quarters.
FY27 capex about INR500-odd crore for the full year (H2 lower than H1's INR363.8 crore, though one large deal adds capex). FY28 capex likely near INR600 crore or slightly more.
FCFO-to-EBITDA conversion expected in a 1.2x-1.5x range.
PAT margin hovering in 7%-10% range going forward; EBITDA margin range of 20%-23% for next year, depending on capacity timing.
Largest-ever deal to be announced next quarter; expected to require significant capex on a single asset.
capex_capacity: Desks at 145,300 across 85 centres in 8 cities (+27% YoY); ~11,700 desks added in Q2 (record), ~18,400 in H1, ~4,500 more in October.
Bengaluru 54,000 desks (anchor); Hyderabad 20,000 (now second-largest, overtook Mumbai); Pune 17,000.
Q2 additions: Chennai ~3,600 desks (managed office extension), Hyderabad ~2,700 (WeWork-branded), Pune ~2,600 (managed offices).

Pipeline: 9,000+ desks under signed leases and fit-out, ~38,000 seats under LOI; total ~47,000 incremental seats (32% above current capacity). Management cites a further ~2 million sq ft of prospective space not yet at LOI stage.
Growth centres (open <12 months) hold ~25,000 desks; portfolio breakeven occupancy 55.7%. Refurbishment cycles expected around year 5-7 per asset.
demand_pricing: Revenue-to-rent multiple at an all-time high of 2.7x; new large managed-office deals are at about 3x, driven by higher capex per sq ft.
Contracted escalations of 6%-7% on existing contracts; renewal rate about 80%-85% in H1 FY27; churn lower than expected.
Average commitment term rose to about 28 months (larger accounts ~32 months).
Locked-in core revenue grew ~66% to INR3,843 crore against INR1,421 crore of rent, about 2.7x coverage (management also cites ~2.9x in Q&A).
Enterprises 77% of core revenue; GCCs ~41% of mix; other global companies ~26%; Fortune 500 ~30%; top 10 members 23% of revenue.
Minimum wage increases in Karnataka near 60% and backdated BESCOM energy tariffs pressured opex per sq ft in H1; management says margin would be ~22%-23% without these.

qa_highlights.question: How has underwriting changed for new centres (payback, revenue-to-rent) given rising competition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is taking larger positions in Grade A assets, underwriting buildings under development, and doing multi-property deals; it says underwriting is smarter but not drastically changed versus two years ago. Payback periods are improving and capex control is driving better returns.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal trends and pricing on renewals versus new contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal rate 80%-85% in H1; renewal escalations are lower than contracted escalations and pricing on fill-up, as management trades price for loyalty and scale. Around 50% of customer growth comes from existing members expanding.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation between expansion and FCF, and use of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: More FY28 expansion is planned with additional capex; the company is also looking at buybacks or dividends once book losses are cleared, and at investing in adjacent businesses that help Indian companies scale.

qa_highlights.question: Customization revenue in Q2 and EBITDA flow-through; GCC hiring outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization was about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA; management says large lumpiness is normalised. Management sees GCCs continuing to set up in India and expects demand to grow, with premium managed offices and more amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Will March 2027 desk target of 155,000 be met, and what H2 margin uplift to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Already at about 150,000 desks; 155,000 visibility by March, though some deliveries may slip into early April. Margins to expand further in Q3 and Q4, with the larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire. Q4 YoY margin change expected to be modest given a strong Q4 last year.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance for next year and pipeline beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise percentage guidance; FY28 EBITDA margin range of 20%-23%, depending on capacity timing. Pipeline: about 2 million sq ft of additional prospective space not yet signed; leases signed about 12 months out with ~95% visibility, 70%-80% at 18-24 months.

risks_watch: Opex inflation: Karnataka minimum wage hikes near 60% and BESCOM backdated energy tariffs; margin outlook depends on it.
Depreciation rising with the largest capex cycle; PAT margin guided at 7%-10%.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia (~1.2 million sq ft built-to-suit campus in Manyata, a customer for ~7 years) is expected to move out; timing uncertain. Another possible lumpy move-out next year.
Promoter pledge still outstanding; management says it will reduce it over time, with no block sale at current prices, and has three years to repay the debt.
Capex upside risk if more managed-office deals are signed; one very large deal to be announced next quarter.
Desk target of 155,000 by March 2027 could slip into early April.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed on demand, occupancy, margins and cash generation. Cautious on forward margin and capex numbers, with ranges given and direct refusals to guide a single percentage. Evasive on the promoter pledge timing, saying it will come down only when pricing makes sense.
key_quotes: Demand is keeping pace with our largest openings. Our platform is compounding beyond the desk, and margins, returns, and cash, all strengthening throughout the build.
Locked-in core revenue grew nearly 66% to about INR3,843 crores, covering the INR1,421 crores of rent locked in against it, which is about 2.7 times.

We are in no hurry to close it, because we have three years to basically sort of like pay that debt off, and clearly the business is growing faster than the cost of capital that we have for that debt.
So, capex would possibly be closer to the INR600 crores mark, or maybe even slightly more than that for FY28.
